text:
24-hour news summary

1 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5704) Nicolas Bustamante urged empathy for people disoriented by AI’s rapid progress and the loss of crafts tied to identity and meaning.

2 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5705) A policy paper by more than 20 experts called for governments to track how much AI contributes to AI research and warned of potentially massive AI research capacity.

3 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5706) TechCrunch introduced Tab, a personal AI assistant emerging from stealth.

4 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5707) ChatGPT announced a Meetings plugin that records notes, summaries, and follow-up tasks for Pro and Business users on macOS.

5 A commentator argued that OpenAI’s model is demonstrating novel mathematical research ideas rather than merely recombining known techniques.

6 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5709) Antonio Orvieto criticized the mass release of AI-generated mathematical solutions as reducing inspiring mathematical work to a resource-driven race.

7 Google expanded its SynthID Detector partnership with OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao, and Apple to improve transparency around AI-generated media.

8 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5711) Parallel Systems raised $100 million to scale autonomous electric rail vehicles for long-distance freight transport.

9 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5712) Living Models used Gemma 4 and BOTANIC-1 to identify a climate-resilience mutation in melons from 2,494 candidates in one afternoon.

10 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5713) Elon Musk said SpaceX’s Grok bot will use whichever leading backend model best suits each task, including Claude, Midjourney, and Suno.

11 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5714) A trending X page was shared without additional commentary.

12 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5715) Liquid AI released Open d1, open-weight multimodal decision models designed for real-time use from data centers to edge devices.

13 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5717) Russ Salakhutdinov humorously described senior researchers claiming ownership of every successful new AI idea after it works.

14 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5718) Higher-Order Extraction was launched to deterministically derive required numbers from raw webpage values, even when the answer is not explicitly shown.

15 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5719) OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 and an Intelligent UI in ChatGPT, adding more visual answers and interactive tools.

16 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5720) Anthropic introduced Claude Haiku 5.5, calling it its fastest, cheapest, and most capable small model, with substantially lower operating costs.

17 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5721) NVIDIA announced that Jaguar’s Type 01 vehicle uses its Hyperion computing platform and Halos safety system, backed by extensive software testing.

18 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5722) A project demonstrated compiling a biological brain into a browser-running Cadence network that simulates a fish at higher efficiency than a spiking model.

19 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5723) XPU Grasshopper, an AI-co-designed chip, was announced with claims of an 816-fold speed increase over 13 weeks and an FPGA developer-kit preorder.

20 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5724) Microsoft announced local AI capabilities for Windows, including MAI-Code-1.1 Flash, local Copilot handoffs, on-device actions, and secure agent execution.

21 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5725) OpenAI reportedly tested whether its models’ military answers comply with international humanitarian law and the Geneva Conventions.

22 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5726) Luis Garicano argued that frontier labs are reducing pretraining because data is becoming scarce and are shifting toward reinforcement learning.

23 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5727) A mathematician questioned what ordinary researchers should pursue if AI can handle proof discovery and proofreading cannot become a satisfying career.
 (1/2)
